entry.title: Update strict_min_version in the browser_specific_settings example
entry.content:
Description

The first example on the browser_specific_settings page declares data_collection_permissions together with "strict_min_version": "58.0". That combination is not valid: data_collection_permissions is only supported from Firefox 140 on desktop and Firefox for Android 142, so AMO reports "Manifest key not supported by the specified minimum Firefox version" for such a manifest.

This updates the example so it is self-consistent: gecko.strict_min_version is now 140.0, and a gecko_android block with strict_min_version 142.0 is added for the Android requirement. Only that example is changed.

Motivation

Readers copy this example into their manifests and then hit signing warnings. Fixes #44136.

Additional details

Versions come from browser-compat-data (webextensions.manifest.browser_specific_settings.gecko.data_collection_permissions: Firefox 140, Firefox for Android 142).

entry.title: chore(deps): bump fast-uri from 3.1.7 to 3.1.9
entry.content:
Bumps fast-uri from 3.1.7 to 3.1.9.

Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

What's Changed

  • ci: enable trusted publishing releases (v3.x) by @​mcollina in fastify/fast-uri#229

Full Changelog: fastify/fast-uri@v3.1.8...v3.1.9

v3.1.8

⚠️ Security Warning

This security release fixes the following medium-severity security advisory:

  • GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj — inconsistent host case normalization via percent-encoded octets

Users of the v3.x release line should upgrade to v3.1.8.

Full Changelog: fastify/fast-uri@v3.1.7...v3.1.8

Commits
  • 0def703 Bumped v3.1.9
  • a1d0da2 test: generate only relative path references
  • 9eb8759 fix: preserve relative paths in suffix and relative resolution
  • 54c30f7 docs: note suffix-reference authority ambiguity
  • 39e6493 fix: escape a first-segment colon in suffix references

  • ddfc6a5 fix(SEC-03): reject non reg-name characters in domain hosts

  • eb483b5 test: cover colon-first relative references in normalization
  • b110a35 fix(SEC-02): preserve meaning of relative references during normalization
  • Additional commits viewable in compare view

entry.title: [Technical review] Add BiDi network pages: `addDataCollector`, `disownData`, `getData`, `removeDataCollector`
entry.content:
Description

  • Added pages for the following commands of the network module:
    • network.addDataCollector
    • network.disownData
    • network.getData
    • network.removeDataCollector
  • Added a "Data collectors" section to the network module landing page.

Every example was run against Firefox Nightly 160 and Chrome 155 (through ChromeDriver) with a local server, and both browsers behaved the same unless noted below.

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-addDataCollector
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-disownData
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-getData
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-removeDataCollector

Related issue

Doc issue: mdn/mdn#851

Compat quirks worth looking into:

Firefox

  • removeDataCollector collector. BCD shows the collector parameter, the command's only parameter and a required one, as unsupported, while the command is supported since Firefox 143. In my test run, Firefox removed collectors with it, and answered unknown IDs with no such network collector.
  • getData for data: URLs. For a fetch() of a data: URL, Firefox returned the URL's data as written instead of the body the page received: %5B%7B%22id%22%3A1%7D%5D for data:application/json,%5B%7B%22id%22%3A1%7D%5D, and W3siaWQiOjF9XQ== for data:application/json;base64,W3siaWQiOjF9XQ==, where the page received [{"id":1}] (seen in my test run; Chrome returned [{"id":1}] for both). BCD shows getData's data_url feature as supported since Firefox 146, with no note.

/cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.

Chrome

  • getData and disownData versions. BCD shows both commands as supported since Chrome 126, but network.addDataCollector, without which there's no data to get or disown, and all their parameters since 140.
  • Data types:
    • BCD shows the response value of addDataCollector's dataTypes parameter as unsupported, but Chrome collected response bodies in every case of my test run.
    • BCD shows both values of disownData's dataType parameter (request and response) as unsupported, while the parameter itself is supported since 140. In my test run, Chrome released request and response bodies with disownData.
  • addDataCollector maxEncodedDataSize. BCD shows this required parameter as unsupported. In my test run, Chrome rejected 0 and values over 200000000 with invalid argument, but collected a 20,000-byte response with a maxEncodedDataSize of 10000, which the spec doesn't collect.
  • getData for a body still arriving. The spec has getData wait until the whole body has arrived. In my test run, Chrome answered getData sent after network.responseStarted, while the server was still sending the body, at once with unknown error ("No data found for resource with given identifier"). BCD shows getData as supported since 126, with no note.

/cc @OrKoN for the compat sheet update.

entry.title: Enhance input[id] attribute description with links
Clarify the role of flex formatting contexts
entry.content:
Description

Clarify that preventing floats from intruding and preventing margin collapse are related to the flex formatting context established by a flex container.

Motivation

Refer to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Block_formatting_context#:~:text=Flex%20and%20grid,suppress%20margin%20collapsing.

Because these two sentences appear close together, readers may assume that establishing a containing block is what prevents floats from intruding and margins from collapsing. However, these behaviors are actually due to the flex formatting context established by a flex container, not the containing block itself.

Would it be better to explicitly state that a flex container establishes a flex formatting context to avoid confusion? 🤔

entry.title: Update web/api/htmlvideoelement/requestvideoframecallback/index.md
entry.content:
This edit corrects page's example application which unfortunately produces a garbled output for fps. To compute fps, the edited app uses a metadata.presentedFrames field data instead of local var paintCount used by original code and incremented manually in each callback function call. The fps calculation is restricted to the first-time playback; video controls are disabled for this run to simplify the logic of calculation. Metadata are presented as in original app.

Description

This edit corrects page's example application which unfortunately produces a garbled output for fps. To compute fps, the edited app uses a metadata.presentedFrames field data instead of local var paintCount used by original code and incremented manually in each callback function call. The fps calculation is restricted to the first-time playback; video controls are disabled for this run to simplify the logic of calculation. Metadata are presented as in original app.

Motivation

The original example on this page fails to compute frame-per-sec value for a video clip viewed. The calculation on the page produces a garbled output. This bug is trivially corrected with the help of metadata info, but the code becomes complicated if the purpose is to compute fps on the fly while accommodating every user action as pause-seek-replay. So, I restricted the fps calculation to an undisturbed first-time playback that runs from the beginning to the end of the media. To present the most of information, I log the calculation results to the page for every frame of the media which admittingly helps user understand the procedure more clearly. The metadata printout, as in the original application, accompanies this first-time and further playback runs to help the user study how user action reveal itself in the metadata content.

entry.title: [Technical review] Add BiDi `network.continueResponse` and `network.provideResponse` pages
entry.content:
Description

  • Added pages for the following commands of the network module:
    • network.continueResponse
    • network.provideResponse
  • Added a "Changing responses" section to the network module landing page.

Every example was run against Firefox Nightly 160 and Chrome 155 (through ChromeDriver) with a local server.

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-continueResponse
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-provideResponse

Related issue

Doc issue: mdn/mdn#851

Compat quirks worth looking into:

Firefox

  • continueResponse cookies. In my test run, Firefox added a Set-Cookie header for each cookie but kept the response's own Set-Cookie headers, so a response that set theme=dark set both cookies. The spec removes the response's Set-Cookie headers when headers isn't specified. BCD shows Firefox's cookies parameter as supported since 131.

/cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.

Chrome

  • provideResponse statusCode. In my test run, a request blocked in the responseStarted phase got a success from provideResponse with only statusCode: 202, but the page received the server's response with the 200 status. BCD shows Chrome's statusCode parameter as supported since 126.

/cc @OrKoN for the compat sheet update.

entry.title: Document max*In*Stage limit adjustments and update relate Fx rel notes
entry.content:
Description

Firefox 159 fixes a bug whereby previously, maxInStage limits (see GPUSupportedLimits) were adjusted to the values of maxPerStage limits, but those adjustments were not correctly reported in the device limits.

Those adjustments are now correctly reported. See https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2006720, particularly the comments from https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2006720#c26 onward.

This PR updates the 151 and 159 rel notes to accurately document the situation at each stage. It also adds a section to the GPUSupportedLimits page to explain this adjustment. It's a bit of a weird situation, and hard to understand, and I've tried my best based on the info I've been given.

entry.title: docs(http,api): document origin-keyed agent clusters by default
entry.content:
Closes #46194

Under WHATWG HTML PR whatwg/html#7617, agent clusters are specified to be origin-keyed by default.

This PR updates the documentation:

  1. \ iles/en-us/web/http/reference/headers/origin-agent-cluster/index.md:
    • Clarifies that modern browsers enable origin-keyed agent clusters by default (?1).
    • Documents \Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?0\ as the explicit opt-out mechanism to relax execution context back to site-keyed isolation.
    • Adds example for \Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?0.
  2. \ iles/en-us/web/api/document/domain/index.md:
    • Clarifies under failures that setting \document.domain\ is ignored by default in modern origin-keyed environments unless explicitly opted out via \Origin-Agent-Cluster: ?0.

cc @domenic for review as offered in #46194.
